skill.name: using-neon
skill.description: Guides users through Neon Serverless Postgres setup, connection choices, docs lookup, CLI workflows, APIs, Auth, and SDK references.
skill.summary: Use official Neon guidance for Serverless Postgres setup, drivers, APIs, CLI workflows, and best practices.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around reference paths and package names. The skill does instruct agents to use curl against Neon documentation, which is a real but limited external command and network egress risk.

remediation.issue: The skill tells agents to use curl for documentation lookup.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer platform-approved documentation retrieval tools, or require user confirmation before running curl from the skill instructions.

remediation.issue: Documentation fetching depends on live external content from neon.com.
remediation.suggestion: State that only official Neon documentation URLs should be fetched and avoid using user-supplied URLs as command targets.

remediation.issue: The package references many local reference files that are not present in the scanned file tree.
remediation.suggestion: Include the referenced files or revise SKILL.md so marketplace users receive complete guidance without broken references.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable guidance for Neon setup, drivers, CLI workflows, and APIs. This skill routes Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to focused Neon guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Neon Serverless Postgres for database setup and best practices.
Directs users to verify Neon claims against official documentation before answering.
Shows how to locate Neon documentation through the llms.txt index and markdown pages.
Organizes guidance areas for features, getting started, connection methods, and developer tools.
Lists topics for Neon drivers, Drizzle ORM, Auth, JavaScript SDK, CLI, Platform API, and SDKs.
limitations: The scanned package contains only SKILL.md, so referenced local files are not present here.
It does not connect to a Neon account or inspect a real database by itself.
Current product details may require live access to official Neon documentation.
CLI and API guidance still requires user credentials, permissions, and project context.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Neon Project
use_cases.description: Choose setup steps, connection strings, dependencies, and schema planning for a new Neon-backed application.

use_cases.title: Select Runtime Connection Options
use_cases.description: Compare driver and connection choices for serverless, edge, and long-running backend environments.

use_cases.title: Prepare Operational Workflows
use_cases.description: Map Neon CLI, Platform API, branching, autoscaling, and recovery topics before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Neon App
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a new Neon Serverless Postgres project for a Node.js app. Include setup steps and documentation to verify.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Connection Method
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Neon connection options for an edge function, serverless function, and long-running backend. Recommend one option for each runtime.

prompt_templates.title: Design Branching Workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Neon workflow for preview branches, schema changes, autoscaling, and instant restore for a small SaaS team.

prompt_templates.title: Automate Platform Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a CI workflow that uses Neon CLI or Platform API for branch creation, migrations, and cleanup. Include security checks.

output_examples.input: Which Neon connection option should I use for Vercel edge functions?
output_examples.output: A concise recommendation that compares HTTP and WebSocket options, explains runtime fit, and points to official Neon driver guidance.

output_examples.input: How should my team use Neon branching for pull request previews?
output_examples.output: A workflow outline covering branch creation, migration order, preview lifecycle, cleanup, and documentation checks.

output_examples.input: What should I review before using the Neon Platform API in CI?
output_examples.output: A checklist for credentials, project permissions, branch naming, cleanup rules, rate limits, and official API references.

best_practices: Verify product details with official Neon documentation before giving final guidance.
Choose connection methods based on runtime, latency needs, and pooling requirements.
Keep Neon credentials outside prompts and use approved secret storage for CLI or API work.
anti_patterns: Do not guess Neon documentation URLs when an official index or reference is available.
Do not expose database URLs, API keys, or connection strings in shared chat history.
Do not assume one driver or ORM fits every serverless, edge, and backend runtime.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps with Neon Serverless Postgres setup, connection choices, features, CLI workflows, APIs, Auth, and SDK topics.

faq.question: Can it access my Neon database?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance only. Any real database access requires user-provided tools, credentials, and approval.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why does it mention official documentation?
faq.answer: Neon product details can change. The skill instructs assistants to verify answers against official Neon documentation.

faq.question: Does the scanned package include all referenced files?
faq.answer: No. The scanned package only includes SKILL.md, so referenced local files are not present in this copy.

faq.question: Is there any security concern?
faq.answer: The main concern is optional curl-based documentation fetching, which creates limited external command and network access risk.
